itens.titulo: Dólar recua com pesquisa eleitoral no radar
itens.descricao: Dólar recua com pesquisa eleitoral no radar CNN Brasil
trechos: O Ibovespa operava em alta nos primeiros negócios desta sexta-feira (9), com o mercado avaliando novas pesquisas eleitorais sobre o segundo turno que mostraram o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à frente de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na disputa presidencial.
Às 10h08, o índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro subia 0,75%, a 207.765,03 pontos.
O contrato futuro do Ibovespa com vencimento mais curto, em 14 de outubro, tinha alta de 0,39%.
No mesmo horário, o dólar à vista caía 0,43%, aos R$ 5,0020 na venda.
Na quinta-feira, divisa americana à vista fechou a sessão com variação positiva de 0,17%, a R$ 5,0240.
Às 11h30, o Banco Central realiza seu leilão regular de rolagem de swap cambial, com oferta de 50.000 contratos para 3 de novembro.

itens.titulo: AMD Turned $10,000 Into More Than $1.2 Million. Can It Happen Again?
itens.descricao: AMD Turned $10,000 Into More Than $1.2 Million. Can It Happen Again? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - AMD's Data Center revenue doubled to $6.72 billion in Q2, with OpenAI and Anthropic each committing gigawatts of AMD GPU capacity.
- AMD's base case returns just 1.29% by 2031, as a $1.06 trillion market cap makes repeating a million-dollar run nearly impossible.
Someone who put $10,000 into Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) at the end of 2011, when shares closed at $5.40, would have about $1,202,629 at the most recent close of $649.42.
The last 10 years alone produced a 9,314.81% gain, enough to turn $10,000 into $941,481.
AMD now trades at $656.10, and the AI data center buildout is the main story behind it.
So what could $10,000 invested today be worth by 2031?
What $10,000 Could Become by 2031 In the base case, a $10,000 investment in AMD could be worth about $10,129 by 2031, a total return of 1.29%.
That rests on a projected five-year share price target of $664.58, which works out to an annualized return of just 0.26%.

itens.titulo: Here's What $10,000 Invested in JPMorgan Chase When Jamie Dimon Became CEO Is Worth Now
itens.descricao: Here's What $10,000 Invested in JPMorgan Chase When Jamie Dimon Became CEO Is Worth Now Yahoo Finance
trechos: 1, 2006, and has now served as the company's top executive for more than two decades.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Continue » Dimon's leadership has helped power strong returns Since Jamie Dimon became JPMorgan's CEO, the company's stock has risen by roughly 730%.
If you invested $10,000 in the company's stock on the day that he became the company's leader, your holdings would now be worth roughly $83,020.

For comparison, the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: SPY) has risen roughly 524% over the same stretch -- and $10,000 invested in the exchange-traded fund (ETF) and held across the duration of Dimon's tenure would now be worth approximately $62,420.
The bank has paid a dividend for 29 years running, issuing a direct cash payout to shareholders every year of Dimon's tenure, and currently has a 15-year streak of annual payout growth.

With dividends factored in, JPMorgan has delivered a total return of roughly 1,320% since Dimon became the company's CEO -- enough to turn a $10,000 investment held across the stretch into approximately $141,540.
